thread.title: Senator Moody introduces bill to prevent financial aid fraud targeting ghost students
thread.title_full: Senator Moody introduces bill to prevent financial aid fraud targeting ghost students

author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Senator Moody introduces bill to prevent financial aid fraud targeting ghost students
text:
Senator Ashley Moody announced on Apr. 29 the introduction of the bipartisan No Aid for Ghost Students Act, which aims to address financial aid fraud by preventing so-called “ghost students” from obtaining federal student aid using stolen or fake identities. Senators Tommy Tuberville and Maggie Hassan joined Moody in introducing this legislation.
The proposed bill seeks to strengthen identity verification and oversight in the federal student aid process. “Taxpayer-funded student aid should go to students—not fraudsters gaming the system. This legislation takes common-sense steps to verify identity, strengthen oversight, and ensure federal dollars are not wasted,” said Senator Ashley Moody.
Senator Tuberville also supported the initiative, saying, “Our young students work night and day to earn their spot on campus. Zero federal student aid should go towards ghost students who are stealing money from Americans. As Co-Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions task force to root out waste, fraud, and abuse in education, I am proud to introduce this bill and will not stop until we eliminate all fraud.”
Senator Hassan highlighted concerns about evolving scam tactics: “Scammers are deploying increasingly sophisticated tactics to steal money and federal financial aid from hardworking Americans. In the face of these scams, we need to do more to protect students and taxpayer dollars. This bipartisan bill will require that the federal government establish an identity fraud detection system during the student financial aid process, catching scammers on the front-end before tax dollars leave the government’s bank account. I will continue to combat the scourge of scams and ensure that higher education is accessible for all Americans.”
According to details released with the announcement, amendments would require both educational institutions and the Department of Education (ED) to use an identity fraud detection system when reviewing FAFSA applications flagged for possible fraudulent activity. The ED must notify applicants if their application raises suspicion of identity fraud as well as inform designated institutions listed on those applications.
Institutions would be required either through in-person or live audiovisual means to verify flagged applicants’ identities before any funds are disbursed; they must then notify ED upon completion of verification while maintaining records according to information provided by Senator Moody’s official website. Additional requirements include establishing guidelines for these procedures at institutional levels as well as reporting annually on system effectiveness.
Moody has a background volunteering with domestic violence victims while practicing law according to her official website. She serves on several Senate committees including judiciary; homeland security; health; education; labor; pensions; as well as joint economic committee according to her official website. Moody is a fifth-generation Floridian who grew up in Plant City with family ties in law enforcement according to her official website.
The Department of Education recently launched a new capability aimed at detecting FAFSA-related fraud.
